note: FIXTURE ONLY. The key material in this file is public test data. It must never be used for a real credential or to protect real data.
payloadSerialisation: payloadJson is the exact plaintext that was sealed: UTF-8, compact (no whitespace between tokens), keys in payloadKeyOrder, "/" not escaped, newlines inside privateKeyPem escaped as \n. Absent userHandle or displayName are written as JSON null, not omitted. A writer should emit this shape; a reader must parse the decrypted JSON and not compare its bytes, since records sealed by another encoder may differ in escaping.
sealedLayout: base64 (standard, padded) of nonce (12 bytes) + ciphertext + tag (16 bytes); AES-256-GCM, AAD = UTF-8 of aad.
aadLayout: aad is the UTF-8 bytes of version|recordId|databaseId|createdAtEpochMs|rpId|credentialId|usernameB64, joined with "|" and built from the envelope fields. createdAtEpochMs is written in decimal, credentialId is the envelope string as is (unpadded base64url), and usernameB64 is the unpadded base64url of the username UTF-8 bytes (aadUsernameB64 here), so a username containing "|" cannot make two envelopes share an AAD. The envelope rpId, credentialId and username are plaintext so records can be listed and matched without decrypting; they are authenticated by the AAD, so altering any of them makes the seal fail to open. After opening, a reader must also check that the payload rpId, credentialId and username equal the envelope values and treat any mismatch as an unreadable record.
